Relevant facts, in short, are that the opposite party No.1, Sonali Bank as plaintiff instituted a suit being Title Suit No.44 of 1991 on 11-3-1991 before the Artha Rin Adalat, Dhaka praying for realisation of Taka 5,47,51,652 from the defendant-opposite party Nos.2-8 by selling the mortgaged property. The opposite party Nos. 2-6 and 7 as defendant Nos.1, 4 and 5 contested the suit by filing a joint written statement denying most of the allegations of the plaint. The present petitioner, Bangladesh Shilpa Bank Ltd. was defendant No. 7, who also contested the suit by filing a written statement. 

 (d) where the suit appears from the statement in the plaint to be barred by any law [:] 1 

 "It appears that after the application made under Order VII, rule 11 read with section 151 of the Code, learned Assistant Judge examined witnesses thereupon and came to a finding that the consideration for the deed was Taka 1,10,000. The course adopted by the trial Court is unknown. The proceeding initiated under section 96 of the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act, 1950 is a summary one. Such application for preemption can never be termed as a plaint. Further, taking evidence upon such application for deciding the consideration of the transfer is serious abuse of process of the Court".
